html:
A pivotal moment in Middle East geopolitics is unfolding with an imminent agreement between Iran and Oman to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan have formalized a new mutual defense pact amid a US-Israel war on Iran and escalating regional turmoil. This intricate dynamic sets the stage for potential shifts in global energy markets and security alliances.

Middle East Security: A new "Mecca Joint Defence Pact" has been signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan, pledging mutual defense, with Pakistan stating an attack on one amounts to an attack on all. This alliance emerges amidst escalating conflict in the Middle East and a US-Israel war on Iran, prompting analysts to consider its implications for the US role in the region. Concurrently, US and Omani officials expect a deal "soon" to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, though Iran states the reopening depends on US commitments and may involve transit tolls, while a senior military advisor said Iran will not allow a second corridor in Hormuz. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf asserted that the US strategy of threats and broken promises has failed, and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian condemned the "mentality" in Washington on the anniversary of the Hiroshima and Nagasaki bombings.

US Affairs: On the domestic front, President Trump has signed new orders targeting birthright citizenship and efforts to end "birth tourism." A federal appeals court halted construction of Trump’s $400 million White House ballroom project, which Trump claimed was a "national security threat." US President Donald Trump also reportedly admitted to serious ammunition shortages in the US army. The nomination of Todd Blanche to lead the Department of Justice faces hurdles, with Senators Lisa Murkowski and Bill Cassidy expressing concerns. Separately, Hunter Biden, the former president's son, told the BBC his pardon was "not good" for America or his father's legacy, also revealing his father's cancer has spread. Former Virginia congressman David Brat was confirmed by the US Senate as the next US ambassador to Australia.

European Migration: A rare spat between EU nations escalated as Spain imposed temporary border controls on visitors from Italy, retaliating against similar measures by Rome. This follows an influx of about 78,000 migrants from Morocco into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta, creating significant "irregular migration pressure." Meanwhile, Lithuania's border guards reported discovering tunnels used by migrants trying to enter from Belarus, raising suspicions of destabilization efforts.

Global Security: US intelligence agencies warn that Putin could test NATO's resolve with provocative actions or a limited incursion, potentially aimed at fragmenting the organization. This comes as Ukrainian President Zelenskyy made his first visit to Russia-friendly Serbia, seeking more arms, while Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic hopes to score points with the EU. In Yemen, Houthi attacks killed at least 10, including government forces and civilians, targeting the oil-rich Marib province, and wounded 11 civilians in Saudi Arabia, fueling fears of a wider regional conflict.

Humanitarian & Social Issues: The Democratic Republic of Congo is grappling with its largest Ebola outbreak on record, with cases surpassing 4,000, and the Africa Centres for Disease Control plans to deploy a vaccine for a previous Ebola strain. In Sudan, hundreds of thousands of civilians in el-Obeid face relentless drone strikes, critical water shortages, a cholera outbreak, and high rates of sexual violence, with the U.N. warning of mass atrocities. A deadly school shooting in Thailand left at least seven people dead after a 14-year-old opened fire at his home and school, prompting the Thai PM to vow stricter gun laws.
